svg.text: A request becomes a validated change.
Five stages. The model is called only where judgement is needed.
Create an isolated workspace, then build and test the untouched baseline.
A failing baseline is caught before the model touches the tree.
jj workspace · cargo check · cargo test · baseline recorded
Brief → spec → architecture → tasks, then a strict YAML plan.
A plan that does not parse fails before code exists. The plan is the contract.
The model implements one task. Build and test decide whether the loop continues.
A pass exits to HARDEN; a failure is fed back as context, not a crash.
fail → back to the coder with the error
A second pass improves the change, then independent checks try to break it.
Refactor, behaviour check, end-to-end tests, intent audit, security scan.
One writer to main. Build on a shadow branch first, then land and validate.
A failure on main reverts to the pre-landing hash and returns the work to the fixer.
WHY WAIT TO TEST ON MAIN?
The workspace is not the product.
Testing there hides three failure modes:
Tests on main use the real schema;
a workspace run must not mutate it.
Shadow first. Lock, move, validate, revert on failure.
One task, one tool loop, bounded retries.
No prompt on a gate. A gate cannot be talked out of a failure.
They send no prompt and grow no context.
A gate guarantees the check ran, not that the code is good.
Drawn from run-20261028-095922 · 28 steps · 21 LLM calls · 6 model-served steps · 22 deterministic tools and gates
